title: Reservoir Dogs
events_chronological: Undercover officer Freddy Newandyke rehearses a fabricated anecdote about a drug bust in a commode with his handler Holdaway until he can tell it like a memory.
Freddy performs the commode story for Joe Cabot, Nice Guy Eddie and Mr. White, and is taken onto the crew as Mr. Orange.
Vic Vega walks out of prison and reports to Joe and Eddie, who owe him for the years he kept his mouth shut.
Over breakfast the crew argue about what "Like a Virgin" is really about and whether waitresses deserve a tip.
Joe hands out the colour aliases and Mr. Pink objects to being Mr. Pink.
The robbery collapses within a minute, and Mr. White shoots his way clear of the police from the getaway car with Orange beside him.
Fleeing on foot, Mr. Orange hijacks a car and is shot in the stomach by the terrified driver, whom he shoots dead.
Mr. White drives the screaming Orange to the warehouse rendezvous, cradles him and swears he is not going to die.
Mr. Pink arrives, argues that the job was a setup with an informer inside it, and hides the diamonds outside the building.
Mr. Blonde strolls in and produces a kidnapped patrolman, Marvin Nash, from the boot of his car.
Left alone with the bound officer, Mr. Blonde dances to "Stuck in the Middle with You", cuts off his ear and douses him in petrol.
Mr. Orange shoots Mr. Blonde dead from the floor and tells Nash that he is a cop and that the police are waiting outside for Joe.
Nice Guy Eddie returns, listens to Orange's account of Blonde, and shoots Nash dead himself.
Joe arrives, names Mr. Orange as the rat, and Mr. White refuses to believe him and turns his gun on Joe.
The three-way standoff leaves Joe, Eddie and White all shot, with only White and Orange still breathing.
Orange confesses that he is a police officer, White shoots him as the police storm the warehouse, and White is cut down.
syuzhet_notes: The film's present tense is the warehouse. Told-order bullets 4, 6 and 9-12 are flashbacks, each announced by a character-name title card - "Mr. White", "Mr. Blonde", "Mr. Orange" - that hands the backstory to whichever man has just walked into the room. The film opens on the diner and cuts straight from it to the bleeding aftermath.
fabula_notes: The interior of the jewellery store, including Mr. Blonde's shooting of the staff, is described in dialogue but never dramatised, so it is not listed as an event; only the escape from it is shown. The weeks between Freddy's recruitment and the job are elided entirely.
